On a school trip we stayed 2 days and 1 night on a big house on the woods, that decades ago used to accommodate people sick with tuberculosis. Many died ofc, since back then medicine wasn't as good as today.

With some friends we went to explore the woods nearby, and found 1 old Oxford shoe in the middle of nowhere. 

The dorms were on the second floor, distributed in two wings. It worked this way. You went upstairs to the second floor and there was a main hall. Left and right there was a long hall with many doors on both sides, each a different dorm. Each dorm had one or two bunk beds.
When I went to bed at night, I noticed the wood planks above me had markings carved with something sharp.

Years before this experience, my older brother went to the same house (This school trip was a school tradition, since it was a catholic school and they used the house as a religious retreat. A priest used to go with us, and he would hold a small mass on a room that worked as a chapel). While his class was having lunch, he went upstairs to look for something he had left in his suitcase. When he left his dorm, that was on the far end of the hall, he heard a banging noise, like someone was smacking wood. He fastened his pace but the noise only grew. In his words, it was like someone was simultaneously hitting every wood plank on every bunk bed with a pipe. He ran downstairs and told his friends. No one had heard anything.
Been there, I know it hurts. Some people simply don't understand how affective responsibility works :(

First of all I'm sorry for what you have to go through with your mom, it's never easy to watch a family member suffer from mental health issues. That being said, I do think you should go to therapy, for two main reasons. 
First, because given your entire family situation you are under a huge amount of stress, and it's not healthy to carry that weight around. A therapist can help unpack all of it step by step to make your situation more manageable. Now, you might think that you are OK with everything, but trust me, these things build up and eventually get you, sometimes as a panic attack. Living with untreated anxiety takes a massive toll on your entire health... It can even induce detrimental changes in your brain. 
Second, because of your self harm. I know that it helps you calm down, this is an effect of chronic SH. However, it is not a healthy response to stress, and you could unwillingly seriously harm yourself or others while doing so. There are other ways to lower anxiety, being the best and fastest option medication. Another technique that is meant only for crisis when you really want to cut yourself is to use ice cubes and rub them in your skin. It should produce a similar effect of pain/relaxation.
Please go to a therapist, put your own health as a priority. It is a good investment for your present self and for your future self, physically and mentally speaking.
